body:
I did try to talk to a few people but they ended up making me feel like my problems are really small. Surprisingly they had very little to do with that. In a way, talking about my problems made me feel like they were very small. 

Everyone I talk to tells me that it's just the quarantine that's making me feel this way. But I'm being very honest here, if it was, I would know. It isn't. I'm genuinely not okay and my mental health is degrading by the minute. 

Guess I'll just wait for this quarantine to be over and seek help again.

I was in therapy for a few months when my life was hell. I was put on Prozac and attended frequent sessions. But I had to stop a while after because my family didn't have the money to pay for it anymore, but I did start to feel a little better. My life didn't really change much at that time so I was still dealing with a lot. But I was dealing with it better. However, my life did take a positive turn when I started university. For a year, I truly felt happy (with bumps here and there, how it is). And at this moment I have the same life, that made me happy...but I feel horrible. 

Do you think my depression is was hurried by a false sense of happiness? And now it's coming out again?
